record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
record.context_brief: Relativistic extension of ab initio calculations
record.original_question: How can nonrelativistic ab initio nuclear approaches such as Green’s Function Monte Carlo calculations, which are currently limited to light nuclei, be extended or connected to the relativistic momentum and energy transfers encountered in accelerator neutrino beams so that they contribute to a complete CCQE description?

evidence.quote:
They employ a pa-
rameterized version of the nucleon-nucleon interaction (VA18), including 3-body
forces (TNI), and solve for the low-lying states of the nucleus using quantum
Green’s Function Monte Carlo (GFMC) techniques. The computational com-
plexity of such an approach is currently limited to light nuclei ( A≤ 12).

The approach of the NUCLEI collaboration is necessarily non-relativistic
and serious questions were raised at the workshop as to how to extend this
work to the momentum and energy transfers encountered with neutrino beams

While there are domains where a non-relativistic treatment may suﬃce,
it is clear that a complete picture of the CCQE process will require a
thorough accounting of relativistic eﬀects.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an ab initio many-body description of a nucleus with mass number A, in which the ground state and low-lying excited states are obtained from a realistic two-nucleon interaction (e.g., Argonne v18) supplemented by a three-nucleon interaction, with eigenstates and electroweak response functions computed via Green's Function Monte Carlo (GFMC). Such a treatment is intrinsically nonrelativistic and, due to its computational complexity, is currently feasible only for light nuclei (A ≤ 12).

In charged-current quasi-elastic (CCQE) neutrino–nucleus scattering at accelerator energies, the leptonic vertex transfers four-momentum (q, ω) whose magnitude routinely lies in the relativistic regime, where the struck nucleon's final momentum is comparable to or exceeds its rest mass.

Problem: Formulate a systematic framework that extends or connects nonrelativistic GFMC-type ab initio calculations of nuclear electroweak response functions to the relativistic kinematic regime characteristic of accelerator neutrino beams. Specifically:

(a) Construct a Lorentz-covariant (or appropriately boosted) prescription for the hadronic tensor W^{μν}(q,ω) that reduces, in the limit |q|/M_N → 0, to the GFMC nonrelativistic response functions, while incorporating the correct relativistic single-nucleon current and kinematics at large |q|.

(b) Specify how two-body meson-exchange currents and final-state interactions, presently treated nonrelativistically in GFMC, are to be promoted to the relativistic setting in a manner consistent with current conservation and gauge invariance.

(c) Provide quantitative criteria, in terms of |q| and ω, delimiting the kinematic domain in which the proposed extension reproduces nonrelativistic GFMC results and the domain in which relativistic corrections dominate, and demonstrate convergence to known relativistic limits (e.g., the relativistic Fermi gas or relativistic mean-field response) at high |q|.
artifact.category_tag: Ab initio nuclear response functions for neutrino scattering
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made: Rocco et al. (Phys. Rev. C 97, 055501, 2018) developed a relativistic treatment of ab initio electron-nucleus scattering using a factorization (spectral function) approach informed by GFMC, and Nikolakopoulos et al. (Phys. Rev. C 109, 014623, 2024; arXiv:2304.11772) introduced a two-fragment-model boost to a frame minimizing nucleon momenta, extending GFMC neutrino-nucleus calculations to higher |q|. These are partial solutions: a fully relativistic, gauge-consistent ab initio framework valid throughout the accelerator-neutrino kinematic range, including two-body currents and final-state interactions, is still under active development.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic effects in Green's function Monte Carlo calculations of neutrino-nucleus scattering
status_evidence.snippet: By performing calculations in a reference frame that minimizes nucleon momenta and utilizing the two-fragment model, the applicability of GFMC calculations of neutrino-nucleus scattering can be extended to higher momenta than currently possible.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work extends GFMC neutrino-nucleus calculations to higher momentum transfers via frame choice and two-fragment model—partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic effects in ab-initio electron-nucleus scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Rocco et al. develop a treatment of relativistic effects in ab initio lepton-nucleus scattering using factorization with GFMC-derived spectral functions.
status_evidence.claim: A factorization scheme connecting ab initio nonrelativistic input to relativistic kinematics has been formulated.

status_evidence.title: Ab initio Calculations of Lepton-Nucleus Scattering (Frontiers in Physics)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of microscopic calculations of neutrino-nucleus cross sections; nonrelativistic nature of methods is a recognized limitation that recent approaches partially address.
status_evidence.claim: The relativistic extension is recognized as ongoing and only partially achieved.
